header.title: Semantic Model Structure
header.description: Four distinct but interconnected ontologies that provide comprehensive software engineering governance across application portfolios, enabling strategic initiatives like modernization, rationalization, and greenfield development.

foundation.title: Foundation Principles
benefits: Modality-Agnostic Foundation: Functional ontology represents user needs independently of implementation
Physical Implementation Layers: Design, Architecture, and Code ontologies handle concrete implementations

operational.title: Operational Principles
benefits: Formal Relationships: Cross-ontology mappings enable traceability and governance analytics
Independent Operation: Each ontology operates independently while maintaining structured relationships

ontologyDetails.description: Detailed breakdown of each ontology's structure, purpose, and examples.

functional.title: Functional Ontology
functional.subtitle: Modality-Agnostic User Needs
functional.description: Structure: Persona → Outcomes → Scenarios → Steps → Actions. Purpose: Represents what users want to achieve, independent of how it's implemented
functional.example: "E-commerce Shopper" → "Complete Purchase" → "Buy Gift" → "Search Products" → "Enter Search Term"

design.title: Design Ontology
design.subtitle: Physical UX Implementation
design.description: Structure: User Journeys → Flows → Pages → Templates → Organisms → Molecules → Atoms. Purpose: Defines how user experiences are physically implemented for specific modalities
design.example: "Shopping Experience" → "Product Discovery Flow" → "Search Results Page" → "Product Card" → "Add to Cart Button"

architecture.title: Architecture Ontology
architecture.subtitle: Logical Technical Design
architecture.description: Structure: Layers → Service Types → Services → Entities/Components. Purpose: Logical technical design including services, layers, and system organization patterns

code.title: Code Ontology
code.subtitle: Physical Implementation Units
code.description: Structure: Applications → Modules → Classes/Components → Functions/Methods → Properties/Fields. Purpose: Actual executable code that realizes architecture and functionality

header.title: Design Ontology

layerDefinitions.title: Design Layer Definitions
layerDefinitions.description: Detailed breakdown of each design layer with clear definitions and practical examples.

userJourneys.title: 🎯 User Journeys
userJourneys.description: Multi-session experiences spanning multiple applications or extended time periods
items: Strategic Level: Complete customer lifecycle interactions
Examples: Customer Lifecycle Journey, Employee Onboarding Journey
Spans: Multiple sessions, applications, and touchpoints
Focus: Long-term user relationship and value delivery

flows.title: 🔄 Flows
flows.description: Single-session sequences connecting multiple pages or interfaces
items: Tactical Level: Connected sequences within single sessions
Examples: Registration Flow, Checkout Flow, Data Import Flow
Spans: Multiple pages or screens within one session
Focus: Goal completion and user task success

pages.title: 📄 Pages/Screens
pages.description: Complete screen or interface units representing discrete interaction contexts
items: Structural Level: Complete interface contexts
Examples: Product Listing Page, User Profile Page, API Response Schema
Spans: Single complete interface or data structure
Focus: Complete user context and information architecture

templates.title: 📐 Templates
templates.description: Reusable page-level layout patterns and structures
items: Pattern Level: Reusable structural layouts
Examples: List Template, Detail Template, Dashboard Template
Spans: Layout structure and information hierarchy
Focus: Consistency and reuse across similar contexts

organisms.title: 🧬 Organisms
organisms.description: Complex component groups with specific functionality
items: Component Level: Complex functional groupings
Examples: Navigation Header, Product Grid, Data Table
Spans: Multiple related molecules working together
Focus: Specific functionality and user tasks

molecules.title: 🧪 Molecules
molecules.description: Simple combinations of atoms with single purpose
items: Combination Level: Purpose-built atom groups
Examples: Search Box, Product Card, Form Field Group
Spans: Small groups of atoms with unified purpose
Focus: Single clear function or display purpose

atoms.title: ⚛️ Atoms
atoms.description: Individual interface elements that cannot be broken down further
items: Element Level: Indivisible interface components
Examples: Button, Input Field, Label, JSON Field
Spans: Single HTML element or basic UI component
Focus: Basic interaction and display primitives

header.description: Formal mappings that enable traceability and governance across the four ontologies. These relationships provide the foundation for comprehensive software engineering analytics, consistency validation, and portfolio governance.

implements.description: Design or Code node realizes Functional node
examples: "Add to Cart Button" implements "Add to Cart Action"

supports.description: Architecture node enables Design, Code, or Functional capability

requires.description: Functional node needs specific Design, Architecture, or Code implementation

triggers.description: Functional action initiates Architecture process or Code execution

validates.description: Architecture service or Code unit ensures Functional requirement

patterns.example: User Action → UI Component → React Component

oneToOne.title: One-to-One
oneToOne.description: Single Action maps to single Component or Code unit

oneToMany.title: One-to-Many
oneToMany.description: Single Action implemented by multiple Components or Code units

manyToOne.title: Many-to-One
manyToOne.description: Multiple Actions share same Component or Code unit

adherence.title: Architecture Adherence
adherence.description: % of Code units that properly realize Architecture services
adherence.formula: (Code units with Architecture mapping / Total Code units) × 100

bypass.title: Direct Implementation Bypass
bypass.description: Code units implementing Functional actions without Architecture services
bypass.formula: Count of Functional→Code without Architecture path

fragmentation.title: Service Fragmentation
fragmentation.description: Multiple Code implementations per Architecture service
fragmentation.formula: Average Code units per Architecture service

compliance.title: Design System Compliance
compliance.description: % of Code units that render approved Design components
compliance.formula: (Code units with Design mapping / UI Code units) × 100

patternFragmentation.title: Pattern Fragmentation
patternFragmentation.description: Different Design implementations per Functional action
patternFragmentation.formula: Count of Design patterns per Functional action

rogue.title: Rogue Implementations
rogue.formula: Count of UI Code without Design mapping

designBypass.description: Functional→Architecture→Code exists but no Design mapping

architectureBypass.description: Functional→Design→Code exists but no Architecture mapping

orphaned.description: Code exists without any Functional mapping

conflicting.description: Different Code units for same Functional action via different paths

modernization.label: Application Modernization:
modernization.text: Maintain Functional mappings while updating Design/Architecture/Code

rationalization.label: Portfolio Rationalization:
rationalization.text: Identify duplicate implementations and consolidation opportunities

crossModal.label: Cross-Modal Consistency:
crossModal.text: Ensure equivalent experiences across web, mobile, and API interfaces

standards.label: Implementation Standards:
standards.text: Ensure Code units follow established patterns for similar Functional Actions

complexity.label: Complexity Management:
complexity.text: Monitor Code complexity relative to Functional scope

monitoring.label: Consistency Monitoring:
monitoring.text: Automated alerts for governance violations and architectural drift
